item.title: Design References
item.description:
Reference drawings, engineering details, and technical guidance related to transportation infrastructure and street design.

Bernalillo County Standards#

  • Current Bernalillo County Technical Standards Page

    Provides the County’s maintained development and public-infrastructure standards, standard drawings, drainage and transportation requirements, and technical references used to review and construct improvements in unincorporated Bernalillo County.

  • Complete Bernalillo County Technical Standards — March 28, 2023 (archived PDF)

    Contains the County’s 226-page March 2023 requirements for development review, transportation networks, road geometry, pedestrian and bicycle facilities, drainage, pavement design, traffic studies, construction, and green stormwater infrastructure.

item.title: ABQ Ride
item.description:
ABQ Ride bus service information and data.

Rider Information#

  • ABQ RIDE: Routes and Schedules

    The City’s current route, schedule, detour, and trip-planning information. Consult the official service page before a trip because operational details can change.

Uptown Connect#

  • Uptown Connect Project Page

    Tracks the City’s transit-centered redevelopment of the Uptown Transit Center, including design and construction progress, the transit plaza, affordable and market-rate housing, commercial space, sustainability features, and the anticipated 2026–2028 delivery schedule.

item.title: Area & Sector Plans
item.description:
Historical area, sector, and community plans that explain how Albuquerque neighborhoods, infrastructure, land use, and transportation developed. Many no longer control zoning, but remain important planning-history records.

  • City Area & Sector Development Plan Library

    Maintains the City’s current reference index for adopted historical plans. ABQInfo preserves selected complete plans and adoption records whose context remains independently useful.

Near Heights#

  • Near Heights Community Planning Area Assessment (2022; Accepted 2023 Archived PDF)

item.title: Bike Maps
item.description:
Multi-use trails and paths in Albuquerque.

City Bicycle Maps#

  • Albuquerque Bike Maps

    Provides the current Albuquerque Bicycle and Trail Map, the City’s interactive bicycle map, facility-type guidance, trail-riding guides, and public-art bicycle tours, plus locations where printed maps are available.

  • Albuquerque Bikeways and Trails Map (2026 archived PDF)

    Preserves the City’s 2026 printable bikeways and trails map, showing bicycle boulevards, bike lanes, separated facilities, paved and unpaved trails, transit connections, services, destinations, and riding guidance across Albuquerque.

item.title: Bike Plans
item.description:
City bicycle planning documents and master plans, including current and previous network plans and supporting materials.

Current Bike Plan#

  • 2024 Bikeway and Trail Facilities Plan

    Establishes Albuquerque’s current bicycle and trail network vision, policies, facility recommendations, project priorities, and implementation framework for safer, better-connected active transportation.

    • Combined City Edition (Main Plan and Appendices)

      Preserves the City’s complete 513-page publication in one file, combining the adopted plan with the crossings guide and appendices for convenient archival reference. Official City PDF

item.title: Budget & Spending
item.description:
City budget and expenditure data.

Current Budget#

  • City of Albuquerque Approved Budget, Fiscal Year 2027

    The City of Albuquerque’s adopted Fiscal Year 2027 budget provides citywide revenue, appropriations, department and program details, capital support, performance information, and summary charts explaining where public funds come from and how they are allocated.

item.title: Capital Projects
item.description:
Public works capital improvement projects.

Current Project Data#

  • City Council Current, Neighborhood, and Completed Projects

    Opens the Council’s unusually useful project archive, which organizes current initiatives, district and neighborhood capital work, completed studies, reports, corridor plans, task-force records, and supporting documents.

  • Municipal Development Featured Projects

    The City’s maintained index highlights major transportation, facility, safety, parks, and public-space capital projects, providing an accessible project gateway while the machine-readable project-data endpoint is unavailable.

item.title: Capital Spending
item.description:
Capital improvement spending and projects.

Current Capital Program#

  • 2025 General Obligation Bond Approved Program Book

    Albuquerque’s approved 2025 General Obligation Bond program describes proposed capital investments across the 2025-2034 decade plan, including project scopes, funding categories, public facilities, infrastructure, and implementation priorities.

  • 2025–2034 Approved Decade Plan Summary (archived PDF)

    Summarizes approved capital allocations across the 2025–2034 decade plan by department and biennial bond cycle, showing long-range funding for streets, drainage, parks, transit, housing, facilities, and public safety.

item.title: City Facilities
item.description:
City buildings and facilities.

Public-Facility References#

  • Accessible City Park and Recreation Facilities

    The City identifies accessible parks, recreation facilities, and programs, with an accompanying location map. It is a maintained public-facing resource rather than a static facilities inventory.

item.title: Climate & Environment
item.description:
City and regional climate plans, greenhouse-gas inventories, and durable performance records relevant to Albuquerque.

  • City Climate Action Plan and Implementation Hub

    Maintains Albuquerque’s current climate-plan overview, implementation reports, inventories, updates, and related Sustainability Office work. Archived records below preserve the planning lineage and measured baseline.

Climate Action Plans#

  • City of Albuquerque Climate Action Plan (2009)

    Preserves Albuquerque’s first Climate Action Task Force recommendations, covering greenhouse-gas accounting, buildings, renewable energy, neighborhoods, food, waste, behavior change, and transportation before the City’s later equity-centered plan.

item.title: Dashboards
item.description:
Data dashboards and visualizations.

Project, Program, and Safety Dashboards#

  • DMD Active Projects Viewer

    Maps active and completed Municipal Development projects by phase, category, district, and location, with searchable descriptions covering transportation, traffic engineering, drainage, facilities, and other special projects.

  • DMD by the Numbers

    Summarizes the infrastructure assets maintained by Albuquerque’s Department of Municipal Development, providing a high-level operational inventory across streets, signals, lighting, drainage, and related systems.

  • Street Maintenance Projects Viewer

item.title: Demographics
item.description:
Albuquerque demographic and census data.

Regional Data#

  • MRCOG Socioeconomic Data

    Mid-Region Council of Governments publishes regional population, households, employment, income, commuting, and related planning data. It is the appropriate regional source when a question extends beyond City limits.

  • Albuquerque Neighborhood Data

    The City’s open-data service provides neighborhood geography and associated data resources for map-based analysis, local reference, and comparisons among Albuquerque communities.

  • MRCOG Community Profiles

    Summarizes the central New Mexico region’s population, geography, counties, municipalities, pueblos, transportation connections, and urban-rural context, providing a concise companion to detailed census and socioeconomic datasets.

item.title: Development Process
item.description:
Cross-cutting development process documents, manuals, and reference materials.

Development Process Manual#

  • Development Process Manual (June 2, 2020)

    Provides the City’s technical requirements and procedures for planning, designing, reviewing, permitting, and constructing public infrastructure associated with development projects.

County Development Review#

  • Bernalillo County Traffic Impact Analysis

    Explains when development in unincorporated Bernalillo County requires transportation-impact analysis and connects applicants to the County’s review process, technical expectations, transportation planning, and development standards.

item.title: Maps
item.description:
Interactive maps of city data and infrastructure.

Citywide Reference Maps#

Regional Long-Range Transportation Maps#

  • Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area Boundary Map (2020)

    Maps the official Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area boundary and member jurisdictions used for federally required metropolitan transportation planning, programming, data analysis, and regional coordination.

  • MRMPO Bikeway System Map (2026)

  • MRMPO Pedestrian System Map (2026)

  • MRMPO Roadway System Map (2026)

  • MRMPO Transit System Map (2026)

    These adopted regional maps show the existing and proposed long-range networks used by MRMPO to coordinate bicycle, pedestrian, roadway, and transit planning across the Albuquerque metropolitan area.

item.title: Metropolitan Redevelopment Plans
item.description:
Plans and historical records for designated Metropolitan Redevelopment Areas, where the City uses public investment and redevelopment tools to support housing, infrastructure, business activity, and neighborhood revitalization.

  • City Metropolitan Redevelopment Areas

    Maintains the City’s current index of designated areas, maps, plans, goals, and redevelopment information. The archived plans below preserve records that may be amended, renamed, consolidated, or removed from the live collection.

Current Downtown Plan#

  • Downtown 2050 Metropolitan Redevelopment Area Plan (2025 archived PDF)

item.title: Parks & Recreation
item.description:
Parks and recreation facilities and programs.

Plans and Data#

  • Urban Forestry and Let’s Plant ABQ

    Describes Albuquerque’s urban-forest benefits, the City’s management of roughly 25,000 park trees, the 100,000-tree planting initiative, community engagement findings, planting resources, and current program work.

  • Parks and Recreation Featured Projects

    Maintains the City’s detailed index of active park, trail, aquatics, recreation, and public-space improvements, linking project histories, design concepts, public engagement, schedules, and construction updates.

item.title: Projects
item.description:
Selected major development activity and the plans and datasets needed to understand it. Individual projects belong here when their scale, public impact, planning significance, or unusually useful public record warrants inclusion—not merely because a permit was issued.

Corridor Redevelopment Plans#

  • Bridge Boulevard Corridor Redevelopment Plan (2013 archived PDF)

    Guides redevelopment along Bridge Boulevard in the South Valley by coordinating land use, transportation, streetscape, drainage, economic development, public investment, and implementation strategies for the corridor between the river and Coors Boulevard.

item.title: Public Safety Data
item.description:
Police, fire, and emergency services data.

Current Dashboards and Datasets#

  • ABQ Safety Dashboard

    The City dashboard brings together public-safety measures and reporting in one maintained location. Use it for current, high-level performance information rather than treating a downloaded snapshot as current.

item.title: Rail Runner
item.description:
The New Mexico Rail Runner Express connects Belen, Albuquerque, and Santa Fe. This page combines current rider information with preserved planning, investment, safety, and system-development records that are otherwise scattered across Rio Metro, MRCOG, and NMDOT.

Current Rider Information#

  • Rail Runner Schedules

    Rio Metro is the authoritative source for current schedules and service information. Use it for travel planning rather than a static timetable.

  • Rail Runner Stations and Connections

    Provides current station pages, parking and access information, connecting transit services, and links to rider resources throughout the corridor.

item.title: Safety & Crash Data
item.description:
Bicycle safety statistics and crash data.

Safety Program and Project Map#

  • Albuquerque Vision Zero

    The City’s Vision Zero program page is the maintained source for its traffic-safety approach, performance work, and related materials. It is broader than bicycling, but directly relevant to bicycle safety and street design.

  • Albuquerque Vision Zero Action Plan (2021 Archived PDF)

    Sets Albuquerque’s original 2040 Vision Zero framework across street design, safe speeds, policy, education, walking and rolling, data, and accountability. The City’s 2023 Year-in-Review later replaced it for implementation, but this plan preserves the program’s baseline.

item.title: Speed Management
item.description:
Traffic calming and speed management initiatives.

Neighborhood Traffic Management Program#

  • Neighborhood Traffic Management Program

    Provides the maintained program overview for addressing speeding and cut-through traffic on residential streets, including eligibility, request procedures, current meetings, completed studies, policy documents, and emergency-route constraints.

  • Submit a Traffic Calming Request

    Explains how residents request a City traffic-calming evaluation, what information the application requires, which streets qualify, and where to submit the online or written request.

item.title: Stormwater & Drainage
item.description:
Technical standards, studies, models, and public references for Albuquerque’s drainage, stormwater, erosion-control, and municipal storm-sewer systems.

Hydrology and Development Review#

  • AHYMO-S4-R2 Hydrologic Model User’s Manual (2018)

    Documents Albuquerque’s official arid-lands hydrologic modeling software, including watershed inputs, rainfall, infiltration, routing, detention facilities, sediment, output interpretation, examples, and procedures used in local drainage analysis and development review.

    Official City Hydrology Section · Official City PDF

  • City of Albuquerque Construction Site Manual (2018)

    Sets illustrated inspection standards for construction-site sediment and erosion controls, vehicle tracking, inlet protection, channels, housekeeping, washout, debris, street cuts, curb work, stabilization, and maintenance of required best practices.

item.title: Studies
item.description:
Transportation studies and reports.

City Corridor and Neighborhood Studies#

Central Avenue: 1st Street to Girard#

  • Official City Project Page

    Collects the City’s project history and current authoritative links for the Central Avenue Complete Street Plan and Design Toolkit between Downtown and Girard Boulevard.

  • March 2014 Draft Plan and Design Toolkit (archived PDF)

    Documents existing conditions, public priorities, multimodal design concepts, catalytic redevelopment areas, implementation strategies, and block-by-block recommendations for Central Avenue between First Street and Girard Boulevard.

item.title: Submit Documents
item.description:
Submit Documents#

Email info [at] abqinfo [dot] com to submit documentation to the site.

Information that is not available on cabq.gov or other public sites is prioritized.

For easiest transmission, upload documents to your Google Drive, set sharing to Anyone with the link, and send the link.

item.title: Sun Van
item.description:
Sun Van paratransit service information.

  • City Paratransit Service

    Albuquerque’s official page for Sun Van and related paratransit information, including current eligibility, reservations, service policies, accessibility guidance, and rider resources.

item.title: Traffic Operations
item.description:
Regional roadway operations, traffic analysis, incident management, and intelligent transportation systems.

City Street Operations#

  • Albuquerque Area Street Jurisdictions

    Identifies whether Albuquerque-area public streets are maintained by the City, Bernalillo County, NMDOT, or another entity, with address search and jurisdiction boundaries.

  • Interstate Maintenance Responsibilities

    Maps litter, debris, and landscape-maintenance responsibilities along Albuquerque interstates and freeways, helping users distinguish City, NMDOT, and other operational roles.

  • City Street Speed-Limit Data

    Publishes Albuquerque street speed-limit data as a live GIS service derived from OpenStreetMap, supporting mapping and analysis while requiring users to consider the source’s stated limitations.

item.title: Transportation Plans
item.description:
Regional plans, long-range plans, and other system-level transportation planning documents.

Regional Transportation Planning#

  • ABC Comprehensive Plan, Chapter 6: Transportation (2025 Update)

    The transportation element of the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan guides land use and mobility decisions, covering a multimodal system, safe access, travel choices, coordination, and implementation policies for the city and unincorporated county.

  • MRMPO 2045 Metropolitan Transportation Plan

    Establishes the Albuquerque metropolitan area’s adopted long-range transportation vision through 2045, including regional growth assumptions, multimodal needs, safety and equity goals, funded projects, performance measures, and implementation priorities.

item.title: Zoning & IDO
item.description:
Zoning regulations and Integrated Development Ordinance information.

Current Ordinance and Zoning Tools#

  • Integrated Development Ordinance — Effective May 6, 2026

    The City’s current Integrated Development Ordinance establishes zoning, development standards, and review procedures for Albuquerque. This preserved original is the effective May 2026 release.

    Official City IDO page

  • Interactive IDO Zoning Map

    Search an address or parcel and inspect the mapped zoning layer. Map results should be checked against the effective IDO and City review staff for a site-specific determination.
